tier_reason: B to C: Bazel's only wins are over GNU Make 4.3 run with its default built-in rules, a baseline crippled by a build default (AssemblyScript precedent); Make with -rR and Ninja beat Bazel by 1.8x to over 100x in every incremental and null row (derived from page data). The harness also has one run per cell, an unstamped x86 Bazel binary and a background cache deletion that overlaps the next tool's timed full build.

corrections.workload: Third-party overhead benchmark: N simulated modules (50 to 100,000) whose build rules only touch 0-byte files, measured as full build, incremental build (one most-imported interface file rewritten) and null build (nothing changed), parallelism 4, one run per cell.
corrections.tradeoffs: JVM server process: about 242 MB to 4 GB resident across these runs and about 6 MB to 26 GB of output-base disk (the x86 disk column excludes the install base, the Arm column includes it); slow cold full build; steep learning curve (BUILD/Starlark files, many options); hermetic sandboxed actions with remote cache and remote execution, whose benefits this benchmark does not exercise. Output lands in the user cache directory, not the source tree.
corrections.caveats: Enricher: one run per cell; the x86 Bazel binary is unstamped (no_version); the disk column is inconsistent (x86 excludes the install base, Arm includes it: 6M vs 310M at 50 modules, 26G vs 341M at 100k); generate.sh deletes the old ~/.cache/bazel with a background rm -rf that overlaps the next tool's timed full build; bazel shutdown is never run between tools.

Enricher: measure.py does one pass and never cleans the build directories, so the fastest-of-several-runs figures were taken by hand; on the full-build chart Premake's Make backend (about 12.7 s) nearly matches CMake/Ninja (about 12.5 s), so most of the 20% gain over CMake's Makefile generator is generator overhead. In thutt/build-tool-comparator, Make with -rR ties Ninja 1.11.1 on incremental and null builds and beats it on full builds from 50k modules (x86 100k: 103.8 s vs 407.1 s).
